PADLAB FIELD GUIDE · CONNECTIONS

Connected, but not detected?

By PadLab · Updated October 9, 2026

A controller can be paired with your computer without being visible to a web page. Start with the connection, then check how the browser exposes gamepad input.

Start controller test →

1. Activate the controller on the page

Open the gamepad tester, keep its tab visible and press a physical controller button. Some browsers wait for controller interaction before exposing a device. Clicking the page alone may not activate gamepad detection.

2. Check the USB connection

Use a cable that supports data, not only charging. Try a direct USB port and another known working data cable. A charging light shows that the controller receives power; it does not confirm that inputs are reaching the operating system.

3. Check Bluetooth pairing

Verify that the controller is connected in your operating system’s Bluetooth settings and has enough charge. Follow the manufacturer's pairing instructions for the exact model. A device may reconnect to a console or another computer instead. Compare with USB if you need to isolate the wireless connection.

4. Open the tester directly in a supported browser

Use a current browser that supports the Gamepad API. Open the tester over HTTPS as a normal page. Embedded frames and browser policies can restrict controller access. If the page reports that the API is unavailable or blocked, try another browser and check any relevant managed-device policies.

5. Inspect controller mode and remapping software

Some PC controllers offer XInput, DirectInput or console-specific modes. Those modes may change how the operating system recognizes the device. Follow the controller documentation rather than changing modes at random. Steam Input and other remappers can expose virtual controllers; select the intended device in the tester’s controller menu.

6. Separate detection from mapping

If button numbers and axis values appear, detection is working. A missing standard mapping means the browser has not assigned familiar control positions. PadLab keeps the raw data available and disables the standard stick interpretation. It does not assume that axis 0 is a thumbstick on every wheel, flight stick or unusual gamepad.

7. Compare another application or device

Check whether the controller works in an operating-system controller panel or a known compatible game. If it fails across applications, follow the manufacturer's driver and firmware instructions. If it works elsewhere, record the controller model, operating system, browser version and connection type to narrow down the compatibility issue.

Detected does not mean every feature is exposed.

A browser may receive buttons and axes while omitting vibration, a touchpad, a microphone or a battery reading. PadLab does not claim to test features it cannot access.

Once inputs appear, follow the button test or stick drift test. Technical reference: MDN’s Gamepad API guide.

Find the failing layer

ObservationNext step
Operating system does not see the controllerCheck power, data cable, pairing and manufacturer support.
Operating system sees it; browser does notFocus the HTTPS page, press a physical button and compare a supported browser.
Browser shows raw input numbersDetection works. Investigate mapping rather than reconnecting repeatedly.
PadLab works; one game does notCheck game bindings, device selection and remapping profiles.

Use the input-mode guide before changing controller modes. For an issue report, include steps to reproduce, model, browser/OS versions, connection type and whether USB and Bluetooth differ. Do not include account credentials or unrelated personal information.
